title: ABC Score for Massive Transfusion
sources: Nunez TC et al. J Trauma 2009; Cotton BA et al. J Trauma 2010 (validation)
purpose: A 4-item bedside score (no labs) to predict the need for massive transfusion after trauma and trigger early MTP activation. Score ≥ 2 is the activation threshold.

interpretation.label: Low likelihood of massive transfusion — MTP activation not mandated by the score; continue standard resuscitation and reassess (sensitivity for MT is lost below 2)

Activate the massive transfusion protocol — give balanced product (1:1:1 RBC:FFP:platelets), tranexamic acid within 3 h of injury, calcium, and control the bleeding source. Sensitivity ~ 75–90%, specificity ~ 67–86% for needing MT

notes: ABC ≥ 2 is a trigger, not a ceiling — clinical gestalt, ongoing haemorrhage, or a rising shock index should activate MTP even at a score of 0–1. Recheck as data change (a delayed positive FAST or a falling BP moves the score). Alternatives / adjuncts: shock index > 0.9–1.0, the Revised Assessment of Bleeding and Transfusion (RABT) score which adds pelvic fracture, and lactate / base deficit once available.
buildNote: Additive, 4 items × 1 point. Threshold ≥ 2 activates MTP.
